extractedFacts.premisesPunitiveDamagesStandard: Clear and Convincing Evidence -- Miss. Code § 11-1-65
extractedFacts.premisesPunitiveDamagesCap: Tiered cap based on the defendant's net worth, ranging from $20 million down to $2 million as net worth decreases (small businesses/individuals below a statutory net-worth floor may face no cap at all in some formulations) -- Miss. Code § 11-1-65(3)(a)
extractedFacts.premisesNegligentSecurityTest: Specific Harm Rule ("atmosphere of violence" test)
extractedFacts.premisesModeOfOperationCitation: Wal-Mart Stores, Inc. v. Littleton, 822 So. 2d 1024 (Miss. 2002) (declining to treat store as insurer; requiring proof beyond mere occurrence of harm)
extractedFacts.premisesLiabilityDistinctNote: Mississippi does not enforce a rigid Keetch-style separation between a 'condition' claim and an 'activity' claim; premises cases are analyzed within the traditional status-based negligence framework rather than as a wholly separate cause of action requiring an election of theories.

outcome.description: The jury found the defendants' negligence the sole proximate cause of the fall and awarded $393,000 in economic damages (past and future medical expenses) and $3,000,000 in noneconomic damages. The circuit court reduced the noneconomic award to the $1,000,000 statutory cap (Miss. Code Ann. 11-1-60(2)(b)), entering an amended final judgment for $1,393,000, and denied JNOV or new trial. The Court of Appeals of Mississippi, en banc, affirmed on December 17, 2024, rejecting the dangerous-condition, notice, expert and further-remittitur arguments. No attorney's fees.

source.caseName: Pilot Travel Centers, LLC and Gina Franklin, Individually v. Willa Womack

source.excerptNote: Verbatim from the FACTS (paragraphs 3-5), the defendants' contentions on dangerous condition and notice (paragraphs 8, 15, 18), record facts about the general manager, the vestibule doors and the video recited in paragraphs 21-23, and the orthopedic evidence and pretrial motion practice in paragraphs 32-38. Removed: paragraphs 1-2 and 6 (verdict, statutory reduction, judgment, post-trial motions), all standard-of-review and case-law discussion, the court's analysis and holdings, the expert-qualification rulings, and the damages-remittitur section (paragraphs 46-51, whose only medical-expense figure is stated together with the jury's award).
